title: QUIC All-Upstream Handshake Matrix Architecture
purpose: Describe the advisory all-upstream interop-runner handshake matrix without widening the existing major-peer testcase matrix or support claims.
design_summary: The all-upstream profile builds its hosted matrix from the upstream runner's `implementations_quic.json` at dispatch time. Entries with role `both` or `server` become local-client handshake cells, and entries with role `both` or `client` become local-server handshake cells. The local helper also accepts `-PeerImplementationSlots all` in split-role mode so maintainers can plan the same role-compatible peer sets locally. Client-role cells use the existing known source-length completion boundary when the requested file is mounted locally, and otherwise read the response until peer FIN because runner-generated response bodies are mounted into the peer server container, not necessarily the local client container. The first profile is intentionally handshake-only to establish broad peer discovery and artifact retention before expanding into transfer, retry, keyupdate, resumption, migration, or HTTP/3-adjacent work.
alternatives_considered: Widen the existing `major-peer-matrix` requirement to every upstream slot. Rejected because that requirement intentionally owns a narrow `quic-go` and `msquic` testcase matrix with preserved historical evidence.

Run every currently supported non-HTTP/3 testcase against every upstream implementation immediately. Rejected because the first missing surface is full registry coverage, and testcase expansion should follow after handshake results classify peer compatibility and infrastructure failures.

Add Incursa.Quic to the upstream runner registry for this local proof. Rejected because the request can be satisfied through the existing local replacement-slot model without mutating the upstream checkout or publishing an image.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The hosted profile must remain manual and advisory.
The matrix must derive peer slots from the checked-out upstream registry instead of hardcoding the current list.
Client-only upstream slots must only be peers when Incursa.Quic runs as server.
Server-only upstream slots must only be peers when Incursa.Quic runs as client.
The profile must upload one artifact bundle per role and peer cell.
Client-role cells must tolerate upstream-runner generated source files that are not mounted into the local client container.
Handshake-only evidence must not be described as every-testcase proof or support readiness.
data_and_state_considerations: The workflow generator emits a GitHub Actions matrix from the upstream registry fields `role` and `image`. Each runner cell stores artifacts under `artifacts/interop-runner/<cell>/`, preserving the helper invocation, runner JSON and Markdown output, stderr, testcase inventory, and runner logs when available.
risks: Upstream registry changes can add images that are slow, temporarily unavailable, or incompatible with hosted runners.
A wide peer set can produce mixed failures that need characterization rather than runtime changes.
Readers may overread handshake-only corroboration as broad QUIC or testcase coverage if the advisory boundary is weakened.

supplemental_sections.heading: Matrix Size
supplemental_sections.content: With the current upstream registry shape, the profile generates one local-client cell for every server-capable peer and one local-server cell for every client-capable peer. The exact count is intentionally derived at dispatch time rather than stored as a normative constant.
